items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: We had a fellow named Eddie Burns and they would prowl and over in North Beach, he was Italian, Burns was his stage name, but they had great influence... But they just didn't hire you.

ctx.x: For moralistic of course it’s terrible but from an economic standpoint it just seems silly. Why would they open it in the Western District as you said?

Well the area was, see we were a minority. The black presence and the Japanese presence, we were very small see. Because you had Russian, French, Irish — the Irish mainly were out in the Mission District, but you had all kind of races here, and Caucasian. And so we were in a very small minority. So I guess either they figured they wouldn’t miss it or maybe the white community might resent it. I don’t know what the psychology was or the thinking was behind it. But that was a thing. But see so the same thing, after…
So when this thing happened with the union, it was in ’46 was it?
